## Objective and definition of success

October 4 clarification: prioritize conceptual changes to the reduction
program, not implementation micro-optimizations. In particular, investigate
relations which prevent expensive descendants from being generated and exact
composition which cancels unnecessary intermediate obligations. Use primary
literature to propose mechanisms with small decisive tests. The cluster can
accommodate a second production campaign alongside the current one, but that
is not a reason to launch before a significant improvement is demonstrated.
The user remains responsible for production launch and lifecycle decisions.

Develop a generic, profile-guided optimizer that finds exact parametric rules
which reduce the **shared downstream workload**, rather than merely shortening
individual right-hand sides. Use the frozen five-loop renormalizable-gauge
request as the pressure test: preserve all 116 required queries, 67 helpers,
existing routes, terminals, guards and descendant obligations.

Deliver a runtime-steerable optimization workflow, an independently audited
improved rule pool and a frozen user-launch candidate. Seek a repeatable gain of
at least 20% in completed-cohort downstream work or end-to-end cost on
preregistered representative five-loop validation workloads, without an
offsetting material regression. This is a target, not a promised result.
Require complete four-loop controls and held-out five-loop checks. A smaller
gain may be recorded, but does not by itself complete this ambitious goal.

Do not claim full five-loop closure, eventual termination or an ETA from a
better local metric. Complete scoped closure still means every required query's
reachable obligations are discharged and its reusable output cold-loads.

## Phase 1 — find the actual expensive mechanisms

1. Inventory the stopped historical campaigns and both new live campaigns,
   binding observations to rule-pool identity and a timestamp. Distinguish
   cumulative counters, interval deltas, stale closure snapshots and exact
   finite records. Prefer compact existing exports and bounded reads over
   scanning or duplicating hundreds of gigabytes of checkpoint data.
2. Attribute cost to recurring **rule applications and semantic regions**:
   Apply versus Route work, distinct admitted successors, reuse/containment,
   numerator and positive-power excursions, guard fragmentation, coefficient
   processing and recurrent pinch destinations. Do not present sampled record
   frequency as a full census or invented per-rule attribution.
3. Separate mechanisms: genuinely expensive recurrences, route overcoverage,
   repeated region splitting, broad helpers and already-shared lower work.
   Record root required/helper ancestry as unknown unless actually established.
4. Produce ranked hypotheses and a small representative request panel. Freeze
   discovery/training cases separately from validation and held-out cases,
   including relevant multi-owner context. Select cases from observed work,
   not from where a candidate happens to win.

First deliverable: a reproducible hotspot report, explicit uncertainty and the
first candidate-generation targets. Negative evidence is retained.

## Phase 2 — produce competing exact programs

1. Start with existing bounded exact rule portfolios and source-visitation
   controls. Preserve a common strict-descent ordering when mixing alternatives.
   A different integral ordering is a separate whole-program experiment, not
   an arbitrary per-rule choice.
2. Extend only the missing generic boundary needed to retain/export candidates
   and evaluate them downstream. Keep source generation, candidate authority,
   experimental scoring and artifact publication separate. No topology names,
   loop-count branches or benchmark recognition in the engine.
3. Seek targeted source combinations that cancel expensive successor blocks,
   useful subgraph/symmetry relations and selective translated-source enrichment.
   Revisit rejected Laporta, reflection or dimension-shift experiments only when
   the new profile identifies a concrete different mechanism and falsifier.
4. Favor reusable parametric charts over a catalogue of fixed-point patches.
   Never generalize a sampled benefit or a numerical hit into exact authority.
   Regenerated-source replay, guards, coherent descent and fallback coverage
   remain mandatory. Existing terminals are not changed to manufacture a win.

## Phase 3 — score the shared downstream graph

Build a reproducible, input-driven evaluation loop with a frozen baseline pool,
candidate replacements and unchanged routes, queries, helper context and engine.
Score **union workload after routing and sharing**, not sums of independent
per-target costs. Known-but-unresolved nodes are not free; recorded containment
is not the same as independently established recursive closure.

Use cheap structural scores only to filter candidates. Then use bounded native
lookahead and completed controls to measure newly admitted domains, expensive
Route/Apply work, memory, coefficient cost and exceptional fragmentation.
Include parent application and dispatch; successor-only results are preliminary.
Retain whole-piece alternate dispatch where appropriate to avoid adding splits.

Incomplete probes report unresolved debt, stopping reason and resource usage;
they cannot beat completed runs by stopping early. Fixed-time throughput and
fixed-work cost are diagnostics, not claims of a smaller completed graph.
Use staged exploration, a Pareto set and hold-outs to avoid overfitting proxies.
Measure complete cohorts after combined replacements because individually good
choices can interact badly through shared lower sectors.

## Phase 4 — deepen the search where evidence justifies it

Use campaign feedback to choose the next regions and source families. Once a
downstream evaluator is trustworthy, study bounded cost-to-go estimates or
lookahead-directed source proposals. Compare against FirstValid and the current
structural portfolio. Treat learned/numerical scores solely as heuristics.

Delegate primary-source literature and SpiReD/TIDE inspection around the measured
bottlenecks: targeted elimination, sparse relation selection, recurrence
composition, subgraph/symmetry identities and preservation of correlated domains.
Research must lead to a mechanism, smallest test and explicit rejection rule,
not an accumulating list of untested techniques. Save useful findings in docs.

## Acceptance and deployment

- Focused unit/property tests for every new API and unchanged-policy behavior;
  exact replay, guards, descent, fallback and no unauthorized terminal changes.
- Complete FG/BMW/H/X and combined four-loop controls, with cold reinspection.
- Representative and held-out five-loop tests from the frozen evidence panel;
  full owner/routing/helper context where meaningful, not a favourable isolated
  root alone. Also retain the existing rank-zero control as a regression, not
  a substitute for the full physical numerator request.
- Two matched counterbalanced pairs for promotion candidates, fixed binaries,
  input identity, workers and CPU placement; record host contention, preparation,
  solve/traversal, cold verification, wall/CPU time, RSS and output/work counts.
  First require an A/A run of the evaluator and preregister primary metrics,
  cohort/terminal inventories, cache state and completion/debt checks. Stale
  live closure snapshots and a process exit code are not authoritative completion
  gates; inspect the actual pending work and independent cold result together.
- Distinguish a generation-time cost paid once from application/traversal cost,
  but report both and their amortization. No efficiency claim from busy cores,
  shorter RHSs, fewer masters or a differently restricted request alone.
- Independently audit implementation, mathematics and interpretation. Promote
  only measured useful candidates; leave rejected alternatives documented.
- Freeze a clean candidate executable/rule pool and exact launch instructions.
  Recommend a production switch only after the evidence warrants it. The user
  remains in charge of both running campaigns throughout.

## Progress discipline

Keep CODEX_PROGRESS.md current after material evidence, implementation, audits,
failed tests and commits. Each lane records owner, pending/active/delivered/
rejected/deferred state, evidence paths, measured versus inferred findings and
the next executable step. Keep goals broad enough to improve actual closure
prospects: completing tooling or another frontier patch alone is not success.
